newsitem.title: USA: Rexene agrees to be purchased by Huntsman.
newsitem.headline: Rexene agrees to be purchased by Huntsman.

text.p: Rexene Corp. said Monday the chemical and plastics company agreed to be purchased by Huntsman Corp. in a transaction valued at $600 million.
The acquisition, for $16 a share, also includes the assumption of debt.
Huntsman, based in Salt Lake City, is the nation's largest privately held chemical company. Huntsman-held companies have revenues of about $4.3 billion.
Rexene, based in Dallas, manufactures products for the chemical and plastics industry. It has 19 million shares outstanding.
The deal is expected to be completed in the third quarter of this year.
"We have maintained our interest in Rexene because of the extraordinary synergies and efficiencies that would result from a merger of the two companies," Hunstman Chief Executive Jon Huntsman said.
As a result of the definitive agreement between the two company boards, Rexene has cancelled plans for a share buyback bid and cancelled a special shareholder meeting scheduled for June 12.
The deal gives Huntsman access to the polyethylene business. Chief Operating Officer Peter Huntsman said future growth would be "controlled, but aggressive."
Rexene stock was up 62.5 cents at $15.50 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
